- If sentiment is high (≥0.7) and forecast spikes upward, reduce the peak by 5–10% to avoid overreaction.  
- If sentiment is low (≤0.4) and forecast is rising, cap the forecast at 1–2% below the 14-day moving average to prevent false optimism.  
- When true outcome shows sharp downward correction after a forecast peak, reduce next-period forecast by 3–5% to account for mean reversion.  
- If forecast consistently overshoots true outcome by >3% over 3–5 days, apply a 2–3% downward bias to subsequent forecasts.  
- For 30-day horizon, if sentiment is volatile (alternating high/low), smooth forecast transitions by averaging 3–5 prior values before applying new trend.  
- If true outcome is below 70% of 30-day forecast mean, reduce forecast by 10–15% to reflect risk of prolonged decline.  
- If sentiment drops sharply after a forecast peak, assume downward momentum and reduce forecast by 2–4% per day until sentiment stabilizes.
